title: School, learning and languages
instructionsHu: A vizsgáztató az iskoládról, a tanulásról, a nyelvtanulásról és az oktatási rendszerről kérdez. Válaszolj részletesen, fejtsd ki és indokold a véleményedet.

questions.q: What do you think are the strengths and weaknesses of your school?
Which subject do you think will be the most useful for your future? Why?
What makes a good teacher, in your opinion?
followUps: Can you think of a teacher who inspired you?

questions.q: How do you prefer to learn new things: from books, from videos or by doing them?
Do you think Hungarian students get too much homework? Why or why not?
Which school traditions do you think are worth keeping, and why?
How has learning English changed your life so far?
followUps: What has been the most difficult part of learning it?

questions.q: Would you like to study abroad? What would be the advantages and disadvantages?
Do you think students need private lessons to pass the school-leaving exam? Why?
If you could change one thing in the Hungarian school system, what would it be?

usefulPhrases.en: One of the strengths of my school is ...
She brought the subject to life.
If it were up to me, I would ...

turns.speaker: examiner
turns.text: What do you think are the strengths and weaknesses of your school?

turns.speaker: candidate
turns.text: The biggest strength is definitely the teachers – most of them are really committed, and the language teaching is excellent. The main weakness is the building. It's over a hundred years old, so the classrooms are cramped and the gym is far too small for eight hundred students.

turns.speaker: examiner
turns.text: What makes a good teacher, in your opinion?

turns.speaker: candidate
turns.text: Someone who is strict but fair, and who can explain the same thing in several different ways. Patience matters a lot, too, because not everyone understands a new topic straight away.

turns.speaker: examiner
turns.text: Can you think of a teacher who inspired you?

turns.speaker: candidate
turns.text: Yes, my history teacher. Instead of making us memorise dates, she had us debate historical decisions, and that's actually how I became interested in law.

turns.speaker: examiner
turns.text: Do you think Hungarian students get too much homework? Why or why not?

turns.speaker: candidate
turns.text: Sometimes, yes. The problem isn't one particular subject, but the fact that teachers don't coordinate, so on some days we get homework in five subjects at once. A shared online calendar for homework and tests would solve a lot of this.

turns.speaker: examiner
turns.text: If you could change one thing in the Hungarian school system, what would it be?

turns.speaker: candidate
turns.text: I'd cut down on the amount we have to learn by heart and focus more on practical skills, like critical thinking or financial literacy. At the moment we cram so many facts that we forget them a week after the test.

notes: Feladat teljesítése: a válaszok kifejtettek és kiegyensúlyozottak (erősség és gyengeség is), konkrét példákkal (százéves épület, a történelemtanár vitái), a rendszerszintű kérdésre pedig indokolt, konkrét javaslatot tesz.

Nyelvhelyesség: változatos szerkezetek hiba nélkül – műveltető szerkezet (she had us debate), 'Instead of + -ing', feltételes mód (I'd cut down on …, would solve) és 'so … that' következményes mondat.
Szókincs: pontos, az iskolai témához illő kifejezések (committed, cramped, coordinate, financial literacy) teszik B2-essé a választ.
Érdemes megtanulni: „strict but fair”, „straight away”, „learn by heart”, „would solve a lot of this”.
